mechanisms.name: Amyloid Pathology and Deposition
mechanisms.description: This mechanism involves the abnormal accumulation of amyloid-beta (Aβ) peptides, particularly Aβ42, in the brain. Deposition of amyloid plaques is a hallmark of Alzheimer's disease (AD) pathology and an early indicator that can predate symptoms. Amyloid pathophysiology is detected via CSF testing and PET imaging, and is associated with downstream neurotoxicity, inflammation, and neurodegeneration.

mechanisms.name: Tau Pathology and Neurofibrillary Tangle Formation
mechanisms.description: This mechanism focuses on the hyperphosphorylation of tau proteins, leading to intracellular neurofibrillary tangle formation, which disrupts neuronal transport and function. Elevated total tau (TAU) and phosphorylated tau (PTAU) in CSF reflect active neurodegeneration and are closely linked to cognitive impairment in AD.

mechanisms.name: Neurodegeneration and Brain Atrophy
mechanisms.description: Progressive loss and shrinkage of neurons and synapses, particularly in regions like the hippocampus, entorhinal cortex, and temporal lobes. Structural MRI markers and FDG-PET metabolism changes evidence this mechanism, manifesting as cognitive and functional decline as neurons die and lose connectivity.

mechanisms.name: Cognitive Impairment and Clinical Dementia Expression
mechanisms.description: This mechanism captures the disruption of cognitive domains including memory, executive function, language, and processing speed, translating to deficits measurable by neuropsychological tests and functional questionnaires. It directly accounts for the clinical expression and severity assessment of dementia and MCI.

mechanisms.name: Neuropsychiatric and Behavioral Dysfunction
mechanisms.description: Neurodegenerative changes in key brain circuits lead to non-cognitive symptoms such as depression, agitation, apathy, psychosis, sleep disturbances, and altered behavior. These features are prevalent in AD and MCI and can be measured through structured assessments.

mechanisms.name: Global Clinical Severity and Functional Impact
mechanisms.description: Reflects the overall severity of dementia as it affects daily function, independence, and levels of care required. Combines clinical staging and functional performance in daily activities, as captured by staging scales and caregiver-rated questionnaires.

mechanisms.name: Vascular and Metabolic Contributions
mechanisms.description: Vascular health influences cognition through mechanisms such as ischemia, white matter disease, and neurovascular dysfunction, which can coexist or potentiate AD pathology. Blood pressure, BMI, and metabolic state influence risk and progression.

mechanisms.name: Demographic and Genetic Risk Modifiers
mechanisms.description: Population-based risk factors such as age, education, sex, ethnicity, race, and marital status modulate both risk and progression of AD, potentially through baseline cognitive reserve, socioeconomic factors, and genetic influences.
